newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan chip firms freeze plans amid slump - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Japan chip firms freeze plans amid slump - newspaper.

text.p: Japan's five top semiconductor manufacturers have decided to freeze plans to build new domestic plants in response to a global chip market slump, a business newspaper said on Sunday.

Toshiba Corp., Fujitsu Ltd., NEC Corp. Mitsubishi Electric Corp. and Hitachi Ltd. each would postpone plans to build or start production at factories planned when chip demand was high in 1994-95, the Nihon Keizai Shimbun said.
Toshiba would postpone the start-up of microchip production lines at a 130 billion yen plant in northern Iwate prefecture by one year to 1999, the newspaper said.
Fujistsu would postpone indefinitely the start of construction of a 100 billion yen plant in northern Fukushima prefecture designed to make logic integrated circuits (ICs).

NEC would delay he planned spring start of operations at a custom IC plant in northern Yamagata prefecture to autumn and was considering cutting capital investment at the plant by at least 10 billion yen, the daily said.

Mitsubishi Electric Corp. froze construction of part of its logic IC plant in southwestern Ehime prefecture in January, while Hitachi Ltd. decided to stop operations at its plant in eastern Gunma prefecture, the newspaper reported.
